meta.title: FORGE — Rock Climbing Strength, Power & Conditioning Library
equipment_allowed: Bumper Plates / Lifting Platform (for Olympic-lift variants)

Novice.intensity_power: Light load / low intensity, max movement quality
Novice.grip_work: Submaximal edge depth (20mm+), no max hangs or one-arm work — build tendon tolerance only
Novice.notes: Own basic movement (squat/hinge/press/pull) and build finger-tendon tolerance on large edges before any max-effort hangboard or campus-board work. No barbell work above 65% e1RM, no campus board, no max hangs, no one-arm hangs, no heavy strongman implements.

Beginner.grip_work: Repeaters on 15-20mm edge, submaximal — no max hangs
Beginner.conditioning_intensity: Zone 2-3, ARC/traverse blocks at 60-70% output, technical focus
Beginner.notes: Add posterior-chain, antagonist and core-tension volume. Light strongman carries (farmer's, sandbag) enter the pool for approach-fitness. Hangboard stays repeater-based — max hangs and campus board are not yet introduced.

Intermediate.grip_work: Max hangs on 10-14mm edge 1x/week, repeaters the rest of the week
Intermediate.notes: Campus board (jug/large-rung ladders and bumps only) and max hangboard protocols enter the pool now that tendon tolerance is established. Contrast method (heavy lift + explosive move) becomes the main power tool. Full strongman implements now programmed at moderate loads for approach/general strength.

Advanced.grip_work: Max hangs/one-arm-assisted work programmed and tracked like a main lift, 7-10mm edge
Advanced.conditioning_intensity: Zone 4-5, redpoint-pace intervals at 85-95% output, sport-specific power-endurance blocks
Advanced.notes: Full season periodization (base -> strength -> power -> performance/send phase). Heavy strength and max-hangboard sessions kept 48-72h from projecting or outdoor climbing days. Campus board volume stays low regardless of level — quality over quantity.

Elite.training_age: 6+ years, competing/projecting at a high grade
Elite.intensity_main: 85-97% e1RM, RPE 8-10 only in peak block
Elite.intensity_power: Max intent, autoregulated by movement quality/speed
Elite.grip_work: Fully individualized off actual finger/tendon load data and current project demands, min-edge (4-8mm) work included
Elite.conditioning_intensity: Send-simulation pace, route/boulder-modeled work:rest, autoregulated by session RPE and skin/tendon status
Elite.notes: S&C is fully subordinate to the trip/comp calendar, built backward from the send goal or competition date. Load is set by daily tendon/joint readiness, not the written number — the written plan is a default the coach is expected to override.

session_type_reference.Power / Campus Session: 60-90 min, low volume, full recovery between efforts, never trained fatigued
session_type_reference.Max Hangboard Session: 30-45 min dedicated block, 1x/week from Intermediate, tracked like a main lift
session_type_reference.Power-Endurance / Aerobic Session: 60-120 min, circuit or ARC-style, matched to redpoint/route length
session_type_reference.Strength & Conditioning Session: 45-75 min, barbell/strongman-based, kept 48h+ from hangboard max effort or outdoor days

global_rules: Every session follows this order: power/campus work first -> main strength lift -> hangboard/finger work -> core & body-tension -> antagonist/shoulder-health work last -> power-endurance/aerobic conditioning only on a day NOT preceded by a heavy finger or heavy lower-body session.

Finger and tendon loading is the highest injury-risk variable in climbing — hangboard max-hang protocols and campus board are Intermediate-level-and-up only; Novice/Beginner build tendon tolerance through repeaters on large edges and jug-based substitutes.

Choose ONE discipline emphasis per training block (Bouldering / Sport / Trad-Multi-Pitch) based on the athlete's actual upcoming trip or project rather than developing all equally; Balanced (All-Around) is the correct DEFAULT in off-season or general-prep phases.

Antagonist and shoulder-health work is programmed EVERY session regardless of emphasis or level — climbing's pull-dominant movement pattern makes this the first thing protected, not the first thing cut when time is short.
Deload every 4th week at 40-50% volume reduction for Intermediate and above — finger-specific load is the first variable reduced on a deload, since tendons recover slower than muscle.
Heavy squat/hinge sessions and max-hangboard sessions are placed 48h+ apart, and ideally not on the same day as outdoor climbing or projecting.

Campus board and limit-bouldering (max-intensity, low-volume) work requires a full prior warm-up and is capped at low total volume regardless of level — more sets does not equal more power on the campus board.

Pre-trip / pre-competition taper: finger-intensive work (max hangs, campus board) stops 5-7 days out; only light movement-based power touches remain up to 2-3 days out, then full rest before the send goal or comp.
